_comment: MODEL H (Telugu) architecture. Consumed by common/model.py via GPTConfig.from_json. Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation and are ignored by the loader.
_budget: Target is ~25M trainable parameters. The embedding matrix is INSIDE
that budget, so vocabulary, depth and width compete for one pool:
Untied, the same model is 27,634,944 and over budget. Tying the head
to the input embedding is what makes 12 layers affordable.
_depth_vs_width: One block costs 12 x d_model^2 = 1,769,472 at d_model 384, so every
1,769,472 parameters spent elsewhere is one layer not built. Phase 1
chose an 8,000-piece vocabulary for exactly this reason: 8k affords 12
12 x 384 is preferred to a shallower, wider model of the same size
(e.g. 6 x 544) because attention routes information one hop per layer,
and Phase 3's comparative reasoning -- A > B, B > C, therefore A > C --
is multi-hop by construction. Width buys per-token capacity, which
matters less at 25M than the number of routing steps available.
_positions: Learned absolute (GPT-2 style): nn.Embedding(512, 384) added to the
token embedding. Chosen for being the simplest scheme that is clearly
correct, the easiest to defend, and the cleanest to ablate for the
It caps the context HARD at 512. The table has 512 rows, so position
512 does not exist; and rows never seen in training keep their random
initialisation, so unlike sinusoidal encodings or RoPE this model
cannot extrapolate to a longer context at all. block_size is a
property of the trained weights, not only of this file.
_context_length: 512 tokens, about 1,809 Telugu characters at the measured 3.531
characters per token. Chosen against the compute budget: attention is
O(T^2), and the whole project runs inside a 30 hour weekly Kaggle GPU
quota that has to cover two pretraining runs plus Phase 3 finetuning.
